llm.summary: This skill is a disclosed image-generation CLI wrapper that sends user-provided prompts and selected files to dLazy's hosted API.

dimensions.detail: Network use and file upload are expected for a cloud image-generation service, and the artifact states that only local paths passed by the user are uploaded.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Installation uses a pinned third-party npm CLI, either globally with npm install -g @dlazy/cli@1.2.3 or on demand with npx @dlazy/cli@1.2.3; this is disclosed along with source and homepage metadata.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Trigger phrases include broad image-generation terms and the docs use strong agent wording for running the command and reporting billing/auth errors, but the instructions stay within the skill's stated workflow and do not override safety rules or unrelated user goals.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The CLI can persist a dLazy API key in ~/.dlazy/config.json or use DLAZY_API_KEY per invocation; this credential persistence is clearly disclosed and no background service, privilege escalation, or system persistence is present in the artifact.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The documented purpose is Nano Banana 2 image generation/editing, and the capabilities described are aligned: run dlazy banana2, send prompts/parameters to api.dlazy.com, upload user-specified media to files.dlazy.com, and return hosted image outputs.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install this only if you are comfortable using a third-party dLazy CLI, storing or providing a dLazy API key, and sending prompts plus any explicitly selected local media files to dLazy's hosted service. Prefer npx for non-persistent use if you do not want a global CLI install.
llm.findings:
[AE1] expected: The referenced Chinese skill file is present and was inspected; the cross-link is ordinary bilingual documentation rather than analysis evasion.
[SQP-1] expected: The generic image-generation triggers are somewhat broad, but they match the tool's image-generation purpose and do not add high-impact authority by themselves.
[P9] expected: Manual inspection showed long spaces in Markdown error-table formatting, with no hidden instructions or concealed content after the flagged area.
[SQP-3] expected: The Chinese file contains Chinese error-handling guidance corresponding to the English file; it does not impose unrelated behavior beyond explaining auth and balance errors.
